items.question: Under what conditions must this teaching be kept secret in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching is to be concealed.
Concealment requires deliberate effort.
The context is the mortal world among the lowest of men.
items.inference: This teaching must be carefully hidden in the mortal world among unworthy people.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom may this teaching legitimately be given after proper testing?
premises: The teaching is to be given.
The recipient must be previously accomplished.
The recipient must be tested for one year.
items.inference: This teaching may be given only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text is identified as emerged from Candradvīpa.
The section is numbered as fifth.
The section is called a chapter.
items.inference: This marks the conclusion of the fifth chapter in the text emerged from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the text that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: What understanding has the speaker gained through the grace of the lord of Kaulas?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas.
Knowledge arose by that lord's grace.
What is known is the determination of Kaula.
items.inference: By the lord of Kaulas' grace, the speaker has come to know the determination of Kaula.
items.plain_english: O lord of Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.

items.question: What is the true identity and essential nature of the soul being declared?
premises: The soul is said to be declared.
The question asks who that soul is.
The question asks what the soul's nature is.
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both the identity and the essential nature of the declared soul.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation is requested?
premises: The question asks where dissolution occurs.
The soul is said to go to dissolution.
The speaker requests a complete explanation.
items.inference: The speaker asks for a full account of the locus into which the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the ultimate reality identified as that soul?
premises: The subject is identified as that.
It is described as supreme, partless, and eternal.
It is described as free from disease and stainless.
items.inference: The soul in its highest sense is the supreme, partless, eternal, disease-free, and stainless reality.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul further identified in terms of haṃsa and individual power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme.
That same soul is identified as haṃsa.
It is characterized as the individual associated with power.
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as haṃsa, the individual principle associated with power.
uncertainties: The exact doctrinal sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That soul is supreme; indeed, he is the haṃsa, the individual associated with power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated within living beings?
premises: The subject is the air filled with breath.
It is described as situated.
Its location is in all beings.
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air abides in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam may reflect transmitted phrasing.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called at the very moment it leaves the body?
premises: The subject is that same principle.
The condition is merely leaving the body.
It is then called supreme Śiva.
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, that principle is declared to be supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching said to be received through traditional transmission?
premises: Something is heard as abiding in the ear.
The goddess is addressed.
It has come down through a lineage of tradition.
items.inference: The teaching is heard in the ear as something transmitted through traditional lineage.
items.plain_english: O goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What is the claimed efficacy of merely hearing this knowledge, fair-faced one?
premises: The means is this knowledge alone.
That knowledge is received by hearing.
The fair-faced one is addressed.
items.inference: Mere heard knowledge is presented as having significant efficacy.
uncertainties: The verse states the means but leaves the result to the following verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, heard and received...

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: The practice extends from six months.
One should practice it.
The practiced state is free from bondage.
items.inference: Practicing this bondage-free discipline for six months is prescribed as transformative.
uncertainties: The exact sense of kāṣāyaṃ in this context is ambiguous.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices for six months that state free from bondage...

items.question: What result follows the prescribed practice in relation to disease and yogic company?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases.
Association is with yogis.
The result includes union or meeting together.
items.inference: The practice results in freedom from all diseases and union with yogis.
items.plain_english: He becomes freed from all diseases and attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī regarding the soul's practice?
premises: The subject matter is the practice of the soul.
It has been told to the listener.
Bhairavī is explicitly addressed.
items.inference: The teaching on the practice of the soul has now been communicated to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: What kind of qualified recipient is worthy to receive this teaching?
premises: The teaching is to be given.
The recipient is endowed with all states.
The recipient has a resolved mind.
items.inference: This teaching should be given to one who is fully endowed and firmly resolved.
uncertainties: The case difference between genitive and locative recipients reflects transmitted syntax.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has a firmly resolved mind.

items.question: Why must the essential Kaula teaching originating from the yoginīs not be given indiscriminately?
premises: The Kaula essence is not to be given.
It is identified as the essence of Kaula.
It originates from the yoginīs.
items.inference: The Kaula essence, originating from the yoginīs, must not be given indiscriminately.
uncertainties: The syntactic relation of sambhavam to sāraṃ is slightly compressed.
items.plain_english: The essential Kaula teaching, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after the veil of ignorance is struck away?
premises: The speaker refers to today.
The body is now described as pure.
It was previously struck by the veil of ignorance.
items.inference: The body, once struck by ignorance, is now claimed to be pure.
uncertainties: The form deham appears where a nominative sense is expected.
items.plain_english: Today my body is pure, though it was once struck by the veil of ignorance.

items.question: What auspicious method for overcoming time does the speaker now wish to hear?
premises: The speaker expresses a present wish.
The wish is to hear something.
The topic is the auspicious deception of time.
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear the auspicious method for deceiving time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious means of deceiving time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the possibility of destroying death without doubt?
premises: The speaker declares they will tell.
There is said to be no doubt.
The explanation concerns how death is destroyed.
items.inference: The speaker assures that the means by which death is destroyed will be told without doubt.
items.plain_english: I will tell you, without doubt, how death is destroyed.

items.question: What paradoxical condition affects even the wise at the tip of nectar?
premises: The context involves the tip of nectar.
There is burning by the essence of juice.
Even the wise are affected.
items.inference: Even a wise person can experience burning at the tip of nectar by its potent essence.
uncertainties: The imagery is terse and may be technical.
items.plain_english: Even the wise may feel burning at the tip of nectar by the intensity of its essence.

items.question: How should the practitioner draw in the vital air at the root of tongue and palate?
premises: The locus is the root of tongue and palate.
An action is to be done there.
The air should be drunk slowly.
items.inference: The practitioner should slowly draw in the air at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing oneself at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the air.

items.question: What result follows when this practice is maintained continuously for one year?
premises: The practice is performed for one year.
The condition is that it has been practiced.
Old age and death are said to be destroyed.
items.inference: When practiced for one year, this discipline destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What immunity to venom is claimed for the body of one accomplished in this practice?
premises: Poison does not enter the body.
This holds even if bitten.
The biting agents are great serpents.
items.inference: The accomplished practitioner's body is immune to poison even from the bites of great serpents.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
